sheet-61.description: The main map of the title sheet of the Sea Side Park atlas (Sanborn, 1905), drawn at 120 ft to an inch with north at the top, covering the north end of the borough. It runs from the beach side of Ocean Avenue west to the Barnegat Bay shore, and from M Street north past O Street, Decatur Avenue and Farragut Avenue to the sheet's upper border. Central Avenue crosses it from north to south with the Pennsylvania Railroad track down its middle. The area is almost empty: the large block between O Street and Decatur Avenue holds only the U.S. Life Saving Station No. 13 near Ocean Avenue, and the blocks either side of Farragut Avenue have a boarding house and three small dwellings. South of O Street the blocks between Central Avenue and Ocean Avenue are platted into numbered 25 ft lots with no buildings, and west of Central Avenue only a few lots near the avenue are laid out before the shore of Barnegat Bay, which cuts deeply into the land between O and M Streets. The upper part of the sheet carries the title block, population and water-supply notes and, at left, a key map of the whole town with the sheet numbers 61 to 67; the key map and the title area are not part of this map. The block south of M Street continues on sheet 67.
notes: Farragut Avenue and Decatur Avenue as drawn do not line up with the modern streets of those names (drawn about 40 m south of modern Farragut Avenue, and only about 75 m apart against 150 m today); they were not used as control.
Central Avenue is today a divided road (Northeast and Northwest Central Avenue, NJ 35) on the line of the former railroad.
U.S. Life Saving Station No. 13 between O Street and Decatur Avenue near Ocean Avenue.

Title sheet with key map strip at left (whole town, small scale; left out of the mask) and the main map at lower right, 120 ft to an inch: north end of the town, Farragut Av, Decatur Av, O, N, M Sts between Central Av (Pennsylvania R.R.) and Ocean Av, U.S. Life Saving Station No. 13; Barnegat Bay shore at left. One part.

sheet-62-1.description: Main part of sheet 62 of the Sea Side Park atlas (Sanborn, 1905), drawn at 60 ft to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the right. It shows the south-west corner of the 1905 town between Barnegat Avenue (at the foot of the sheet) and Bay View Avenue along the shore of Barnegat Bay, from 14th Avenue east to 10th Avenue. The Pennsylvania Railroad curves across the blocks between 14th and 13th Avenues to its trestle over the bay at the upper left. Bay View Avenue, 100 ft wide, carries a board walk along its bay side. The blocks are platted into numbered lots and nearly empty: a few dwellings stand near 12th Avenue, and at the corner of 12th and Barnegat Avenues is the private plant of the Sea Side Park Light Water and Sewer Co., with a reservoir, a 30,000 gallon water tank, an engine and boiler house and a gasoline house, together with notes on its wells and pumps and the 8 inch water pipe in Barnegat Avenue. A strip of land between 14th Avenue and the railroad is drawn as a narrow triangular block. The upper right of the sheet is a separate inset (part 2).
notes: Sea Side Park Light Water and Sewer Co. plant (private) at 12th Avenue and Barnegat Avenue.
Bay View Avenue is today South Bayview Avenue.

60 ft to an inch, turned (north to the right). Part 1: 14th to 10th Avs between Barnegat Av and Bay View Av, Pennsylvania R.R. curving to its bay bridge, Sea Side Park Light Water & Sewer Co. plant. Part 2: inset top right, 10th to 8th Avs between Barnegat Av and Bay View Av (continuation of sheet 64).

sheet-62-2.description: Inset in the upper right of sheet 62 of the Sea Side Park atlas (Sanborn, 1905), drawn at 60 ft to an inch with north to the right, like the main sheet. It continues sheet 64 westward: the blocks between Barnegat Avenue and Bay View Avenue from 10th Avenue to 8th Avenue, which do not fit on sheet 64. Two wedge-shaped blocks are cut off diagonally by Bay View Avenue, which runs along the shore of Barnegat Bay with a board walk on its bay side and a narrow strip of lots beyond it. The blocks are platted into numbered lots and show no buildings. The sheet numbers 62 and 64 are printed at the edges of the inset to show where the neighbouring sheets continue.
notes: Bay View Avenue is today South Bayview Avenue; the bay-side junctions were hand-picked.

60 ft to an inch, turned (north to the right). Part 1: 14th to 10th Avs between Barnegat Av and Bay View Av, Pennsylvania R.R. curving to its bay bridge, Sea Side Park Light Water & Sewer Co. plant. Part 2: inset top right, 10th to 8th Avs between Barnegat Av and Bay View Av (continuation of sheet 64).

sheet-63.description: Sheet 63 of the Sea Side Park atlas (Sanborn, 1905), drawn at 60 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the right. It covers the south end of the 1905 town from Barnegat Avenue (top) to Ocean Avenue (bottom) between 14th Avenue and 10th Avenue. Central Avenue, 100 ft wide, runs across the middle of the sheet with the Pennsylvania Railroad in it, and a second line of the railroad curves from Central Avenue near 11th Avenue north-west across the blocks towards the bay bridge on sheet 62. The blocks are platted into numbered lots, nearly all still vacant: there are a few dwellings near 12th and 11th Avenues, one marked as being built, and some outbuildings. Water pipes of 8 and 4 inches are drawn in Central Avenue, 12th and 11th Avenues and along Ocean Avenue, with a note that the board walk lies 75 ft beyond Ocean Avenue.
notes: Central Avenue is today a divided road (Southwest and Southeast Central Avenue, NJ 35); it was not used as control.
Barnegat Avenue junctions were hand-picked at the drawn block edge plus 35 ft (the sheet edge cuts the street).
60 ft to an inch, turned (north to the right): 14th to 10th Avs between Barnegat Av and Ocean Av, Central Av with the Pennsylvania R.R., R.R. curve to the bay. One part.

sheet-64.description: Sheet 64 of the Sea Side Park atlas (Sanborn, 1905), drawn at 60 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the right. It covers the blocks from 10th Avenue to 6th Avenue between Barnegat Avenue and Bay View Avenue (top) and Ocean Avenue (bottom), with Central Avenue and the Pennsylvania Railroad across the middle. A branch of the railroad leaves Central Avenue near 9th Avenue towards the bay. The railroad freight house stands in Central Avenue near 6th Avenue and the depot just beyond it on the edge of sheet 65. North of Central Avenue, near 8th and 7th Avenues, are a coal bin and ice house and a paint shop, and a boat house stands on Bay View Avenue by Barnegat Bay; south of the railroad the blocks nearest Ocean Avenue and 6th Avenue hold most of the sheet's dwellings, with a few outbuildings, and the rest of the lots are vacant. Water pipes are drawn in Central Avenue, 7th and 6th Avenues and along Ocean Avenue, and the board walk is noted beyond Ocean Avenue.
notes: Freight house of the Pennsylvania Railroad in Central Avenue.
The blocks west of Barnegat Avenue between 10th and 8th Avenues are drawn in the inset on sheet 62.
Bay View Avenue is today South Bayview Avenue; Central Avenue (a divided road today) was not used as control.
60 ft to an inch, turned (north to the right): 10th to 6th Avs between Barnegat Av / Bay View Av and Ocean Av, Central Av with Pennsylvania R.R., freight house. One part.

sheet-65.description: Sheet 65 of the Sea Side Park atlas (Sanborn, 1905), drawn at 60 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the right. It covers the centre of the town from 6th Avenue to 2nd Avenue between Bay View Avenue on Barnegat Bay (top) and Ocean Avenue with the board walk (bottom), with Central Avenue and the Pennsylvania Railroad across the middle. The railroad depot stands beside the track near 6th Avenue. The business blocks along Central Avenue have a bakery and confectionery, a bake house, a grocery, a fire house with the hose carriage, a carpenter shop and Union Chapel; the public school is on 4th Avenue north of the railroad. The large hotel The Manhasset fills much of the block between 5th and 4th Avenues near Ocean Avenue, and the rest of the blocks hold scattered dwellings and vacant lots. A cottage named Chopmist stands on Bay View Avenue at 5th Avenue, and the Sea Side Park Yacht Club with its boat house and pier is on the bay shore near 2nd Avenue. Water pipes are drawn in Central Avenue and the cross avenues, and the board walk is shown running along the ocean side of Ocean Avenue, 250 ft from the ocean.
notes: The Manhasset hotel between 5th and 4th Avenues at Ocean Avenue.
Sea Side Park Yacht Club on the bay near 2nd Avenue.
Bay View Avenue is today South Bayview Avenue; Central Avenue (a divided road today) was not used as control.
60 ft to an inch, turned (north to the right): 6th to 2nd Avs between Bay View Av and Ocean Av, depot, Union Chapel, public school, The Manhasset, Sea Side Park Yacht Club. One part.

sheet-66.description: Sheet 66 of the Sea Side Park atlas (Sanborn, 1905), drawn at 60 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the right. It covers the blocks from 2nd Avenue to C Street (Barnegat Avenue) between Bay View Avenue on Barnegat Bay (top) and Ocean Avenue (bottom), with Central Avenue and the Pennsylvania Railroad across the middle. West of North Avenue the blocks are platted into lots with dwellings and boat houses along Bay View Avenue; the hotel The Hiawatha stands at 2nd Avenue and Central Avenue. East of North Avenue two very large undivided blocks, one each side of the railroad, run 620 ft to C Street with only a boarding house and a single dwelling on them. On the beach beyond Ocean Avenue, opposite North Avenue, is the Casino and Pavilion on the board walk, with a row of bath houses on the lots behind it. The board walk turns away from Ocean Avenue at North Avenue and continues north along the beach.
notes: C Street is printed 'C St. or Barnegat Av.'; today C Street.
The Hiawatha hotel and the Casino and Pavilion on the board walk.
Island Avenue and Brighton Avenue, between North Avenue and C Street today, are not drawn (large undivided blocks).
Central Avenue (a divided road today) was not used as control; C Street junctions lie just off the sheet edge.
60 ft to an inch, turned (north to the right): 2nd Av, 1st Av, North Av to C St (Barnegat Av) between Bay View Av and Ocean Av, The Hiawatha, casino and pavilion on the boardwalk. One part.

sheet-67.description: Sheet 67 of the Sea Side Park atlas (Sanborn, 1905), drawn at 120 ft to an inch with north at the top. It covers the northern half of the town from C Street (Barnegat Avenue) north to M Street, between Barnegat Bay with Bay View Avenue along its shore (left) and Ocean Avenue with the board walk and the Atlantic Ocean (right). Central Avenue runs up the middle with the Pennsylvania Railroad, and the Berkeley depot stands beside the track between J and K Streets. The lettered streets C to M cross the island from the bay to the ocean, and the blocks between them are platted into numbered 25 ft lots, almost all vacant. Between J and I Streets near Ocean Avenue are the ruins of the Berkeley Arms Hotel, and a few dwellings stand near Ocean Avenue and at the ends of D and K Streets. The bay shore is irregular, with an inlet cutting in between K and I Streets, and Bay View Avenue is drawn only from I Street south. The blocks north of M Street continue on sheet 61 and those south of C Street on sheet 66.
notes: Ruins of the Berkeley Arms Hotel between I and J Streets; Berkeley depot on the railroad.
C Street is printed 'C or Barnegat Av.'; Bay View Avenue is today North Bayview Avenue.
Central Avenue (a divided road today, NJ 35) was not used as control.
120 ft to an inch, north up: C St (Barnegat Av) north to M St between Barnegat Bay (Bay View Av) and Ocean Av, Central Av with Pennsylvania R.R., ruins of the Berkeley Arms Hotel. One part.
